dus1: Answer yes or no to twelve questions and find out your risk of falling in a minute. The self-assessment checklist the CDC uses with older adults, with scoring and advice on preventing falls.
dus3: Answer “yes” or “no” to twelve short statements and find out your risk of falling in a minute. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) uses this checklist in its programme to prevent falls in older adults. A score of 4 or more suggests you may be at risk of falling. You can share your result with your doctor or physiotherapist.

dus72: This checklist was developed at a geriatric centre of a veterans’ hospital in the US and has been validated as a fall risk self-assessment for older adults. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) uses it in its fall prevention programme. It is not a diagnostic tool; it is a starting point for talking to your doctor about your result.
dus73: My score is below 4. Can I relax?
dus74: A low score does not mean you have no risk of falling at all. It is a good idea to stay active to keep up your leg strength and balance, and to answer these questions again once a year.
dus75: My score was high. What can I do?
dus76: Talk to your doctor about your result; they may want to review your medicines, your eyesight and your feet. Strength and balance exercises are one of the most effective ways to prevent falls. A physiotherapist can put together a programme tailored to you.
